title: Running share of high nights across one invented forty-night record
alt: Line chart of the running share of nights at or above 140 mg/dL against nights recorded. The line sits at zero for four nights, climbs to 0.5 by night ten, then swings inside a narrowing band and reaches 0.65 at night forty, below a flat reference line at 0.70.
longDescription: An invented forty-night record for one late-dinner participant whose per-night probability of a reading at or above 140 mg/dL is 0.70. The first four nights all came in below the cut, so the running share starts at 0 and stays there through night four. It then climbs unevenly: 0.2 at night five, 0.5 at night ten, 0.6 at night twenty, 0.65 at night forty. The flat line marks the fixed 0.70 probability the running share is approaching. Two features carry the lesson. First, early values swing across most of the vertical range, so a short record says little about the underlying probability. Second, the record never compensates for the opening run: by night ten it holds 5 high nights where 7 were expected, and that shortfall of 2 is still there at night 1000, where the count is 698 against an expected 700. The running share reaches 0.698 anyway, because a fixed shortfall shrinks against a growing denominator.
